chunks: He said: Abul Hasan 'Ali ibn Khalid al-Maraghi al-Qalanisi reported to me from Abul Qasim al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan, who reported from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan, who reported from his father, who reported from Ishaq ibn Yazid, who reported from Khalid ibn Mukhtar, who reported from al-A'mash, from Habbah al-'Urani, who said: I heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman

a year before Uthman ibn Affan was killed, saying: "As if I see your mother al-Humayra on an expedition, being led on a camel, and you all clinging to its flanks and tail. With her are the Azd - may Allah admit them to the Fire - and her supporters are Banu Dhabbah - may Allah sever their feet."

He said: When the day of the Camel came and people confronted each other, the announcer of the Commander of the Faithful, blessings of God upon him, called out: "Let none of you initiate fighting until I command you." He said: They shot arrows at us, so we said: "O Commander of the Faithful, we have been shot at." He said: "Withhold." Then they shot at us again and killed some of us. We said: "O Commander of the Faithful, they have killed us." So he said: "Attack, with the blessing of God."

He said: We charged against them and our spears interlocked with theirs, so close that if someone were to walk, he could walk over them. Then the announcer of 'Ali, peace be upon him, called: "Take to the swords." So we began striking their helmets but our swords bounced off. Then the announcer of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, called: "Aim at the feet." He said: We never saw a day with more feet chopped off than that one. He said: Then I remembered the narration of Hudhayfah - "her supporters are Banu Dhabbah, may Allah sever their feet" - and I knew it was a supplication that had been answered.

Then the announcer of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, called: "Go for the camel, for it is surely a Satan." He said: One man wounded it with his spear, and another man cut off one of its legs, so it knelt down and bellowed. Aisha cried out with a loud scream, and her people turned and fled defeated. Then the announcer of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, announced: "Do not finish off the wounded, and do not chase those who flee. Whoever shuts his door is safe, and whoever lays down his weapon is safe."

key_terms.الجمل: Al-Jamal (the Camel) - refers to the Battle of the Camel in 36 AH, named after the camel Aisha rode
key_terms.الحميراء: Al-Humayra (the fair-skinned one) - a nickname for Aisha bint Abu Bakr
key_terms.بنو ضبة: Banu Dhabbah - an Arab tribe that supported Aisha in the Battle of Jamal
key_terms.شيطان: Satan/devil - here referring to the camel as a symbol of fitnah (civil strife)

ai.seo_question: What happened at the Battle of Jamal and what were Imam Ali's orders?
ai.summary: This narration recounts the Battle of Jamal (36 AH/656 CE) through the eyewitness account of Habbah al-'Urani. It begins with a prophecy by Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who predicted Aisha's military expedition on a camel a year before Uthman's assassination. The battle account highlights Imam Ali's extraordinary restraint - forbidding his forces to strike first despite being attacked - and his tactical commands during combat. The narrative culminates in Imam Ali's famous mercy orders after victory, establishing principles of Islamic laws of war.
